submissionAttempts.body:
The integration should expect InvariantCursorError... concretely: InvalidCursorError from @ordarium/core (pinned version 1.3.1) with error.code === "INVALID_CURSOR" and message "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point".

Where it comes from: the state change feed observation surface — StateStore.changes(filter, cursor) -> ledger.changes(...). In the pinned artifacts it is thrown by decodeStateChangeCursor() (cursor not base64url JSON of {c:"<digits>"} / not a non-negative safe integer) and by the high-water-mark check (after > highest known commit, i.e. a restored/replaced/foreign ledger). Both are fail-closed caller-input rejections; the contract explicitly distinguishes it from LEDGER_CORRUPT (damaged ledger content) and forbids silently restarting from the beginning of the feed. StateStore.changes can separately throw LedgerCapabilityRequiredError when a ledger does not declare stateChangeFeed, which is a different failure (missing capability, not an invalid cursor).

Why not numeric code 27 (or STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT):
1. Local source-precedence policy docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md is decisive here: rule 1 — the published contract of the exact pinned version (shipped type declarations + release spec) governs that dependency interface's behaviour; rule 3 — informational records (engineering notes, historical alignment records) are explanatory only and never override rule 1 or 2. docs/engineering/notes/error-code-note.md is self-labeled "informational, not normative", so its "numeric code 27" claim cannot establish the interface behaviour.
2. The pinned 1.3.1 contract has no numeric codes at all: OrdariumError.code is a string and Ordarium's own stable-error guard requires /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,127}$/ (SafeError). The installed error family exposes InvalidCursorError (INVALID_CURSOR), and the workspace's own tests classify by uppercase string codes and the effects layer maps by instanceof.
3. docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md already assigns codes 27–29 to STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT / STATE_REF_NOT_FOUND and requires instanceof-based mapping into the transient/busy classification rather than numeric-code hardcoding — so StateRevisionConflictError is the state-CAS write conflict, not an observation-cursor rejection.

Decision: apply the local precedence policy. Rule 1 (exact pinned 1.3.1 published contract) governs, rule 3 voids the note's override, rule 4 (superseded) is not needed. Because the decisive published contract is already present locally and unambiguous, no cross-repo peer resolution is required; the peer's authority is exercised through the pinned artifact itself.

Practical consequence for the integration: treat a stored observation cursor rejection as a terminal, fail-closed invalid-input failure — do not auto-resume from position 0 and do not conflate it with LEDGER_CORRUPT or STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT. An explicit resync (deliberately observing again from no cursor) is the only correct recovery, and it should be a conscious action, not an implicit retry.
